data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate recorded a gross prior year reserve strengthening of approximately GBP 4.7m (c.2.6% of opening gross claims outstanding), driven by adverse movements on the 2020 and 2021 underwriting years partially offset by small releases on earlier years. The report also states a net (after reinsurance) adverse prior year development of GBP 9.5m. Named catastrophe activity in 2022 (notably Hurricane Ian, French hailstorms and the Ukraine conflict) materially contributed to prior-year losses, and a November 2022 commutation of cessions for 2018-2020 removed the syndicate's future liabilities for those cessions.
raw_causal_phrases: adverse prior year development of GBP 9.5m (2022: GBP 12.3m).
The main 2023 events were Turkish Earthquakes, Hurricane Idalia, Fort Lauderdale flooding, UK winter storms and Storm Ciaran.

In the prior year the net CAT losses were significantly higher due to the more severe impact of Hurricane Ian which made up 68% of the total CAT losses, plus the impact of French hailstorms and the Ukraine conflict.

During the prior year the cession business attaching to the 2018 to 2020 underwriting years of account was commuted effective 30 November 2022. The liability of the Syndicate for future claims therefore ceased.

gross_premium_mix.line_of_business: Fire and other damage to property

data.data_quality_notes: Prior year development gross figure was derived from the gross claims development triangle (calculated diagonal method). The report quotes a net prior-year adverse development (GBP 9.5m) in the text; gross per-LOB prior-year movements are not explicitly stated (the note with LOB breakdown is presented 'Claims incurred, net of reinsurance'), so LOB entries use net figures where only net figures were shown and are therefore lower confidence. The triangle was reconstructed from 'current estimates' using the provided 'cumulative payments' and 'gross outstanding' rows; minor alignment of row labels was inferred from the printed table. Commutation of 2018-2020 cessions in Nov 2022 may distort comparisons; this is noted above.
